title: The Variable Wheeze
summary: Educational demo only—not clinical guidance. Use reversible airflow limitation and airway inflammation evidence to solve a synthetic asthma case.

patient.label: Case A — synthetic patient
patient.presentingComplaint: Educational-only scenario: episodic chest tightness and wheeze after exercise.
history: Symptoms vary from day to day and are worse during pollen season.
No smoking history; symptoms improve after a reliever inhaler.
This fictional profile is for learning and is not a basis for patient care.

content.heading: Variable respiratory symptoms
content.body: Educational-only synthetic history: wheeze, cough and chest tightness vary over time, follow exercise and pollen exposure, and improve after a reliever.

expertBenchmark.name: Respiratory educator benchmark

rationales.asthma-localise: Begin with the conducting airway and localise from the respiratory system to the bronchiole.
rationales.asthma-airway-function: The conducting airway is the structure whose calibre changes in variable airflow obstruction.
rationales.asthma-key-observations: Triggered variability and reversible airflow limitation are the strongest observations.
rationales.asthma-sort-evidence: Separate airflow measurements from inflammatory context before combining them.
rationales.asthma-reversibility: Improvement after bronchodilator supports reversible rather than fixed airflow limitation.
rationales.asthma-mechanism: The inflammatory findings support a type 2 pattern without establishing the diagnosis alone.
rationales.asthma-best-diagnosis: The combined variability and reversibility pattern best supports asthma in this exercise.
rationales.asthma-diagnosis-path: Commit from the integrated pattern, then keep phenotype evidence in a supporting role.

path.label: Orient to the airway
path.detail: Localise the conducting airway before interpreting function.

path.label: Prioritise variability
path.detail: Use the trigger pattern and reversible flow change as the main diagnostic signal.

path.label: Add supporting context
path.detail: Use wheeze and inflammatory evidence to support, not replace, the core pattern.

evidenceWeights.note: Repeated trigger-linked episodes establish symptom variability.
The reversible expiratory-flow change supplies the strongest functional evidence.
The sound sample is compatible with airway narrowing but is not diagnostic alone.

expertBenchmark.diagnosisRationale: Variable trigger-linked symptoms together with reversible airflow limitation form the most coherent authored diagnosis; inflammatory markers and wheeze remain supporting evidence.

debrief.summary: Educational demo only—not clinical guidance. The strongest pattern is variable triggered symptoms plus reversible airflow limitation; inflammatory markers and histology are supportive, not independently diagnostic.

keyEvidence.why: The trigger-linked, variable history distinguishes the pattern from fixed obstruction.
The before-and-after measurements demonstrate reversible airflow limitation.
The expiratory sound supports conducting-airway narrowing when interpreted with the other evidence.
